page: Google Cloud Platform m1-megamem-96 is an x86_64 memory-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon processor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 1434.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of approximately 14.93 GB per core. Cache specifications include 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 38 MB L3 caches. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile characterized by strong multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities alongside weak single-core execution. The server achieves strong results in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth tests, reaching 3918.5 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 201.93 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Conversely, single-core metrics are weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1273.18 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1026.0. Single-threaded operations, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, also fall into the bottom performance tier.

The primary tradeoff of the m1-megamem-96 is its reliance on high-density memory allocation at the expense of single-threaded compute speed. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density for workloads requiring massive RAM footprints without the overhead of local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators. However, for tasks bound by single-core throughput or sequential processing, the hardware configuration may introduce resource underutilization relative to its class.

This server is designed for memory-intensive enterprise applications, large-scale in-memory databases, and multi-threaded data processing pipelines. Its high memory capacity and strong multi-core bandwidth support concurrent database operations and large-scale caching, while its lack of local storage and GPUs makes it less suitable for local-storage-heavy databases or deep learning training.
description: Google Cloud Platform m1-megamem-96 is an x86_64 memory-optimized server configured with 96 dedicated vCPUs from 48 physical Intel Xeon cores and 1434.0 GB of RAM. It features no local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks demonstrate a clear tradeoff: the server delivers strong multi-core CPU performance and high memory bandwidth, but exhibits weak single-core and single-threaded processing speeds. Specifically, the instance excels in multi-core stress-ng tests and large-block memory reads, while single-core Geekbench and compression metrics fall into the lower percentiles. Qualitatively, the server provides high memory density for memory-bound applications, making it a specialized option for workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. It is best suited for large-scale in-memory databases, memory-intensive enterprise applications, and highly concurrent, multi-threaded data processing tasks.
